market_holds: Spot $40.275 (sealed 18:08 UTC), -12.0% over 5 and 20 sessions, 43% below the 52w high. Front-expiry straddle prices a 13.35% move (ATM IV 227%), with call skew richer than puts by ~30 vol points ('upside paid'), put/call OI 1.11 (baseline). Short float 26.3%, 11 days to cover (finviz, 2026-11-19). The week's fall is sector and market tape, not company news: from 11-16 to 11-19 ACN -11.5%, CTSH -9.2%, IT -7.9%, EPAM -6.6%, SPY -2.8%, GLOB -10% (Yahoo daily bars); the only company-specific item was Guggenheim's 11-11 downgrade to Neutral (Middle East weakness, possible loss of work from a large video-game client), -5.5% that day. Consensus is parked on the guide: Q3 revenue $610.7M (17 analysts, range 607.8-613) against a $607-615M guide; Q3 EPS $1.48 against a $1.43-1.53 guide; Q4 revenue $610.2M (16, range 602.6-613); Q4 EPS $1.52. EPS estimates have not moved in 30 days (Yahoo analysis, read 2026-11-19). FY26 guide $2,428-2,462M with a 70bp FX benefit built in (Q2 6-K, 2026-08-13). Last next-open gaps: Q2'26 -6.8%, Q1'26 +9.9%, Q4'25 +2.1%, Q3'25 -3.0%, Q2'25 -9.2%, Q1'25 -31.2%; median about 9% (own arithmetic on Yahoo bars). The stock trades on the next-quarter guide and Glob.AI ARR: the August cut sent it down, and the May hold plus Glob.AI momentum sent it up.
view: Q3 itself will probably land inside the guide. Globant has hit or beaten its revenue range for three quarters, and Q3 currencies averaged about where they stood when the guide was set (EUR 1.151 against 1.153 on 08-12). The print turns on the Q4 guide. Consensus Q4 revenue of $610.2M is flat on Q3 and has not moved, but the dollar has strengthened since late October: EUR 1.098 spot against a Q3 average of 1.151, BRL 5.92 against 5.14, MXN 19.12 against 17.27, GBP 1.310 against 1.344. About 35% of revenue is billed outside USD (FY25 20-F: 64.6% USD). At spot that is roughly a 1.3-1.9% headwind on Q4 against Q3 rates. Add the usual mild Q4 seasonality (about -0.8% QoQ in Q4'25 on my arithmetic), the Saudi weakness management already assumes, and the video-game client risk Guggenheim flagged. A Q4 guide around $598-607M looks likelier than $610M+, which is a 1-2% headline shortfall with the FY held toward the low end. The low end of the FY range only needs about $594M in Q4, so a formal FY cut is less likely than a narrowing. That is a mild negative. Against it: the same currencies weakening (COP, BRL, MXN) lower Globant's Latin American cost base, so margin and EPS should hold or beat, and restructuring cut headcount about 10%. Glob.AI ARR is compounding fast ($32.8M to $52.8M in Q2, at least $110M exit target), and EPAM's print showed the group can be rewarded for AI traction. A 26% short float on a stock that just fell 12% with the sector, priced near 6.5x forward EPS, is set up to squeeze on anything less bad, as in May. Net: a slight downside lean that I would not bet on.
unpriced: Possibly the FX translation into the Q4 revenue guide. The dollar strengthened against EUR, BRL and MXN mostly after 10-27, and Q4 revenue and EPS estimates are unchanged over 30 days, so consensus may not carry the 1-2% headwind. This is a modest effect: margins are partly hedged, investors in the group read constant currency, and the price has already fallen 12% into the print.

recommendation.reason: The one concrete mechanism I found is an FX-driven Q4 revenue guide below a stale $610M consensus. It is worth only 1-2% of revenue and is partly offset by a cheaper Latin American cost base. Crowded short interest (26% of float) and a sector-driven 12% fall into the print give a less-bad outcome real squeeze potential. The direction is not 65% clear either way.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A Q4 revenue guide at or above $610M despite the stronger dollar, or Glob.AI ARR at September of $80M or more with the FY held at the midpoint, would point to a short-covering gap up.

self_critique: The FX headwind is something every covering analyst can compute, and IT-services investors read constant currency, so a translation-driven guide shortfall may not move the stock at all. Meanwhile 26% of the float is short into a stock that fell 12% on sector fear, not on its own news. May 2026 showed the same setup gapping up 10% on a held guide and Glob.AI momentum. Against that, Globant's own history and an ongoing AI-disruption rout in the group could turn any cut into a large down gap. The two tails are roughly balanced, which is why I stay near 50.
